hypotheses.justification:
The statement is still true, and provable, for arbitrary `b : ℝ`; the degenerate cases `b ≤ 0` are absorbed by the junk-value conventions of `Real.rpow` and of `b⁻¹` at `0`.

* `b = 0`: `(0:ℝ)⁻¹ = 0`, so `varthetaScaled 0 z = 0^3 * vartheta (0 • z) = 0` (`varthetaScaled` is `b⁻¹^3*vartheta (b⁻¹ • x)`, Vartheta.lean:59), hence `retainedSmear 0 S x y = 0` and `retainedPressure 0 S x = ∫ y, 0^(5/3) = 0` (`Real.zero_rpow`, `(5/3:ℝ) ≠ 0`). The integrand is identically `0`.
* `b < 0`: `b⁻¹ < 0`, and `vartheta ≥ 0` (`vartheta_nonneg`), so `retainedSmear b S x y ≤ 0`; also `varthetaScaled b z = -varthetaScaled (-b) z` because `b⁻¹^3 = -(-b)⁻¹^3` and `vartheta (-w) = vartheta w` (`vartheta_even`), so `retainedSmear b S x y = -(retainedSmear (-b) S x y)`. For `u ≤ 0`, `Real.rpow_def_of_nonpos` gives `u ^ (5/3) = 0` if `u = 0` and `exp (log u * 5/3) * cos (5/3 * π)` if `u < 0`; here `Real.log u = Real.log |u| = Real.log (-u)` (`Real.log_neg_eq_log`/`Real.log_abs`, `Real.log` is `log |x|` on negatives) and `cos (5π/3) = 1/2` (`Real.cos_pi_div_three` plus `2π`-periodicity, or `Real.cos_eq_cos_add_int_mul_two_pi`). Hence pointwise `u ^ (5/3) = (1/2) * (-u) ^ (5/3)`, and by `integral_const_mul`
  `retainedPressure b S x = (1/2) * retainedPressure (-b) S x`, which by the already-proved `0 < -b` bound (`retainedPressure_nonneg`, `retainedPressure_le_average`, `physicalPressureAverage_le`) is nonnegative and `≤ (1/2) * (-b)⁻¹^2 * (N:ℝ)^(5/3)`.

So in every case `retainedPressure b (S p) p.1` is nonnegative and bounded by a constant `C` independent of `p` (`C = b⁻¹^2 * N^(5/3)` for `b > 0`, `C = 0` for `b = 0`, `C = (1/2) * (-b)⁻¹^2 * N^(5/3)` for `b < 0`). The proof then runs exactly as before without `hb`: measurability of `p ↦ retainedPressure b (S p) p.1` needs only `hS` (`retainedPressure_measurable_param`, which has no positivity assumption on `b`), `hi := integrable_join … (hψ.1 (joinLists s t)).norm.integrable_sq`, `hi.bdd_mul hm.aestronglyMeasurable` with the uniform bound `‖retainedPressure …‖ ≤ C` (using `Real.norm_of_nonneg` instead of the `hb`-dependent `retainedPressure_nonneg`), and finally `Integrable.integral_prod_right`. Only the positivity of `b` was used, via those bounds, and the case analysis above supplies the same two facts for `b ≤ 0`.

(The other arguments cannot be deleted: `hψ` is needed for integrability of `‖ψ.value …‖^2` (take `S` constantly `univ` and a non-square-integrable `ψ`), `hS` is needed for the a.e. measurability of `p ↦ retainedPressure b (S p) p.1`, and `S`, `s`, `t` occur in the conclusion.)
